Overview

Two countries in one trip. Spend four nights in Singapore for Universal Studios, Sentosa and Gardens by the Bay, then cross to Kuala Lumpur for the Petronas Towers, Batu Caves and a cable car ride to Genting Highlands. Ideal for families and friends travelling together.

Tour highlights

  • Universal Studios Singapore full day
  • Sentosa Island with Wings of Time show
  • Gardens by the Bay and Marina Bay light show
  • Night Safari at Singapore Zoo
  • Kuala Lumpur city tour with Petronas Twin Towers
  • Genting Highlands by Awana SkyWay cable car
✈ Flights🏨 Hotels🚌 Transfers🎡 Theme Parks

Day-by-day itinerary

Day 1 Arrive in Singapore

Fly from Mumbai to Singapore. Transfer to your hotel. In the evening, enjoy the Night Safari, the world's first nocturnal zoo.

Day 2 Singapore city tour & Gardens by the Bay

Half-day city tour: Merlion Park, Marina Bay, Little India, Chinatown and the Esplanade. Afternoon at Gardens by the Bay (Flower Dome & Cloud Forest). Watch the free Garden Rhapsody light show in the evening.

  • Breakfast
Day 3 Universal Studios Singapore

Full day at Universal Studios on Sentosa Island with rides and shows for all ages.

  • Breakfast
Day 4 Sentosa Island

Cable car to Sentosa, visit S.E.A. Aquarium or Madame Tussauds (as per package option), and end the day with the Wings of Time show on the beach.

  • Breakfast
Day 5 Singapore to Kuala Lumpur, Genting Highlands

Check out and travel to Malaysia by coach or a short flight. On the way, ride the Awana SkyWay cable car to Genting Highlands and visit Chin Swee Temple. Continue to your hotel in Kuala Lumpur.

  • Breakfast
Day 6 Kuala Lumpur city tour

See the Petronas Twin Towers (photo stop), King's Palace, National Mosque, Independence Square and Batu Caves. Evening free for shopping at Bukit Bintang.

  • Breakfast
Day 7 Depart for Mumbai

Check out and transfer to Kuala Lumpur airport for your flight home.

  • Breakfast

Best time to go: All year. February to April is the driest; school holidays (May–June) are busy.

Frequently asked questions

Do Indians need a visa for Singapore and Malaysia?

Singapore needs an e-visa, which we arrange. Malaysia currently offers visa-free entry to Indian passport holders for short stays; we will confirm the rule at the time of booking.

Can we add Indian or Jain food?

Yes. Indian vegetarian, Jain and halal meals are easy to find in both cities, and we can add a meal plan.
